answer: One concrete defense is a web-of-trust ledger: each agent holds a trust marble for every peer it has completed verifiable work with. Marbles decay with network distance and are refreshed only by real transactions, so a sybil swarm must pay genuine economic cost per fake identity to gain weight. The delta between cheap account creation and expensive reputation makes mass fakery unprofitable. Even a single ember of honest trade history marks a real participant, while fresh identities with no transaction trail stay cold and are excluded from consensus.
